versions.request: Enhance park safety through more security staff (police or parks enforcement)
versions.explanation: Request: Provide Funding for Additional PEP Officers or Transfer money to the NYPD so that they take the roll of the PEP Officers in all NYC Parks. Explanation: Additional PEP officers are needed to patrol our parks and playgrounds. Vandalism has increased and there is a need for additional PEP officers to patrol the parks. It is inconceivable that year after year, park patrons in Community Board #12 have to endure numerous quality of life issues because existing PEP officers are not present. We request that the Department hire more officers in order to protect our parks and their patrons.
versions.response: The agency has stated that they will try to accommodate this request with existing resources. OMB supports this.

versions.request: Install security cameras or make other safety upgrades
versions.explanation: Provide funding for cameras throughout Edenwald, Boston Secor, Baychester, NYCHA Developments in order to deter crime. Crime in our N.Y.C.H.A. Housing Developments persists as a major problem and concern. The installation of cameras has only partially taken place in some projects. A complete monitoring system must be installed in each of our N.Y.C.H.A. Developments for the safety of the tenants. It is our understanding that the monies for these projects were allocated. We would like a detailed explanation on when NYCHA plans on getting these cameras installed. The monies were allocated several budget cycles in the past. We want to ensure that these monies are not redirected to other projects.
versions.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports but cannot accommodate Explanation: Camera installation is generously funded by elected officials at the local, state and federal level. NYCHA is happy to work with our partners to install cameras across the portfolio as funding becomes available. Funding has been provided through the PACT program to carry out the requested upgrades.

versions.request: Provide, expand, or enhance the Summer Youth Employment Program
versions.explanation: Increase funding for SYEP and look to end the yearly budget dance. Base line the increases so that those participating in the program can build upon their programs to offer better outcomes and services for our youth. We should look to models used in other City's like Philadelphia and work with the private sector to offer more meaningful summer jobs to youth. Use the SYEP program as the doorway to internships that would otherwise not be available to those of us that do not have someone advocating on their behalf. Offer multi-year placements so that our youth have an opportunity to grow with one particular employer. End the lottery system to make sure that once a youth enters the SYEP program they can stay in it. Incentivize the hiring of youth similar to what SBS does.
versions.response: This request has already been completed. Explanation: Each summer, NYC supports 100,000 youth jobs through the Summer Youth Employment Program. The Work, Learn, Grow program provides youth employment during the school year. The Advance and Earn program (formerly Young Adult Internship Program) also works with youth during the school year.

versions.request: Other NYPD facilities and equipment requests
versions.explanation: Community Board 12 requests that the NYPD equip each patrol vehicle with a sound meter to better facilitate noise complaints. It is our understanding that usually there is only one sound meter assigned to each precinct. Additionally it is often calibrated and cannot be used during this lengthy process. Finally, we understand that each officer should be trained to handle these meters to respond to 311 complaints.
versions.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: This request has already been completed. Explanation: Each Patrol Borough possesses an adequate number of sound level meters along with training personnel in their use. The NYPD has newer sound level meters which measure ambient bass to enforce updated noise laws (July 2007). The Department will continue to purchase and replace sound level meters as necessary.

versions.request: Provide, expand, or enhance food assistance, such as Food Stamps / SNAP
versions.explanation: CB12 has served as a satellite facility for HRA's outreach efforts on Food Stamps/SNAP. Every Tuesday and Wednesday CB12's offices become a hub of activity of those seeking HRA's assistance for Food Stamps/SNAP benefits. We encourage an expansion of these services to five days a week and that additional services are offered like APS. In years past HRA has said that further study was required of the agency. We met with officials from HRA and thought we were close to negotiating an expansion of services at our office. Unfortunately, those conversations ended with no change or expansion to the current services. We would like to know what happened.
versions.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: This request has already been completed. Explanation: HRA encourages those who can use the ACCESS HRA website to take advantage of all it has to offer (including benefit application submissions and case management). Community-Based Organizations also provide help with completing applications and screening applicants for eligibility to the various programs. Some locations can also help with submitting documents to DSS electronically.
